newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain lashes out at France for attacks on truckers.
newsitem.headline: Spain lashes out at France for attacks on truckers.

text.p: Spain lashed out at France on Wednesday for what it called the passivity of authorities in the face of repeated attacks by French farmers on Spanish truckers transporting fruits and vegetables.
Secretary of State for European Affairs Ramon de Miguel presented Spain's complaint to the European Union in Brussels and asked for measures against France.
"We think bilateral means have been exhausted and unfortunately all this has not been sufficient," Miguel told reporters.
"France is not cooperating sufficiently. It is not diligently complying with obligations to guarantee free circulation of merchants on its territory as would be expected from a member of the Union."
Over the past week, French farmers who want tighter controls on imported produce have been stopping Spanish trucks in southern France to dump and burn their fresh fruits and vegetables.
A Spanish truck driver was in hospital in Montpellier, France after being attacked earlier this week.
Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio said French police were not doing enough to prevent the attacks.
"I suppose they (French police) would not remain so passive if the driver was French," Palacio told reporters in Madrid.
She said Miguel had asked for EU measures "to prevent these types of actions from going on without any type of response or sanctions by the EU".
